subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95 / concurrency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finly.com>, Priya Nair <priya@finly.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95 / concurrency)

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear description of the latency pain and where it shows up in your product. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of pain points (what you shared)
- P95 spikes during peak trading hours: currently observing 600–900ms for inference responses for short prompts (~<256 tokens).
- Streaming UX delays: initial token shows quickly but then token cadence is inconsistent, sometimes with 100–300ms gaps between tokens which breaks your live-update UI.
- Concurrency limits: backend currently tops out around ~80 concurrent generation sessions; when they throttle, tail latency spikes and you see dropped frames in the UI.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Orchestration: Kubernetes on GCP with autoscaling for API pods.
- Model hosting: mixture of OpenAI hosted + internal GPU pool for custom models (quantized).
- Proxying & batching: a proxy service aggregates requests into batches; some custom batching logic in the service layer.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for Finly)
- Non-streaming p95 <= 350ms for typical short responses (<256 tokens) under production-like load.
- Streaming: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) / first token <= 200ms and stable token cadence with <60ms inter-token latency for steady-state streaming.
- Concurrency: handle sustained 80 concurrent sessions with ability to burst to 200 without p95 degradation beyond 10% of baseline.
- Predictable cost envelope (sustained cost per 1M tokens stays within your target).

Immediate next steps
1) We (Redwood) will run an initial profiling test against a small perf harness that mirrors your traffic patterns. Please share a metrics export and a representative prompt set.
2) I've attached our perf template (redwood_perf_template.xlsx) — fill the highlighted sections with your observed p95s / qps and send back.
3) Schedule: propose a 60-min load test window next Wed 2026-06-09 10:00 PT. Please confirm if that works.
4) If the initial test looks promising, we can scope a dedicated reserved capacity trial (2–4 weeks) and a deeper streaming tuning pass (kernel selection + batching + KV-cache warmup).

Open questions we need from you
- Which endpoints are most latency-sensitive (UI stream vs. background generation)?
- Can you provide a short list of 10–20 representative prompts for the streaming flow?
- Do you have quotas or compliance constraints that would push you to a private deployment?

Thanks — I'll loop in Aditya (infrastructure lead) internally for capacity planning once you confirm the dates.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Raj Patel <raj@finly.com>

Cc: Priya Nair <priya@finly.com>, Finly SRE <sre@finly.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 11:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95 / concurrency)

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and aligned on the success criteria. A few clarifications and notes from our side:
- Endpoints: the trading UI streaming flow is the priority (low-latency tokens). Background summarization tasks are less sensitive and can tolerate higher tail latency.
- Representative prompts: we have a set of ~15 streaming prompts I can share; they include templates and variable content lengths.
- Current metrics: attaching an export of last week's p95/p99 metrics and qps by hour (finly_metrics_export.csv). The p95 numbers are spiky during market open/close which is our main concern.

Wed 2026-06-09 10:00 PT works for an initial test window. We'll plan to provide a service account and a temporary test key for the sandbox cluster.

Also: cost sensitivity — we're evaluating whether a dedicated reserved capacity or a mixed routing approach is better. If Redwood can show predictable p95 at a reasonable price, that makes the committed capacity easier to justify.

Thanks,
Raj
Raj Patel | Director of Product, Finly
raj@finly.com

Attachment: finly_metrics_export.csv (CSV stub)

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly latency & streaming requirements (p95 / concurrency)

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending the metrics export. Two small asks before the load test next week:
1) Please drop the 15 prompts into the shared Drive folder (link below). We'll use them as the canonical prompt set for the test.
2) Create a read-only service account and email the key to aditya_rao@redwood.com with a note that it's for the perf test only.

What we'll run next week:
- Baseline run: light traffic to measure cold and warm p95.
- Ramp & steady-state: ramp to your sustained concurrency (80) and then a burst to the target 200 for 5 minutes.
- Streaming cadence check: we'll instrument time-to-first-token and inter-token delta for the streaming route.

After the run we'll share a short report with: observed p95/p99, token cadence histogram, and tuning recommendations (batching, quantization profile, routing). If we meet your success criteria we can discuss reserved capacity pricing and a short dedicated trial.

Proposed time again: Wed 2026-06-09 10:00 PT (60 minutes). Confirmed on our side.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/finly/perf-harness
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/FIN-2026-003

Best,
Marissa
